title: Protect the origin during cold-cache and invalidation storms
businessContext: Every instance recomputes an expensive dashboard simultaneously after a broad invalidation.
problemStatement: Design the system for 10,000 requests/second; a shared homepage cache expires during a deploy. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Avoid cache locks becoming a permanent failure mode.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 10,000 requests/second; a shared homepage cache expires during a deploy
functional: Avoid cache locks becoming a permanent failure mode.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Choose cache scopes and invalidation granularity based on actual read graphs.
A lease owner can crash. Bound lease expiry, prevent obsolete refresh results from overwriting newer versions, and expose refresh queue depth, error rates and served age to operators.
alternativeApproaches: It can hide load by accepting more staleness, but may violate freshness or revocation. Define the product’s stale-service budget and durable source behavior before treating TTL as a capacity strategy.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Send a synchronized cold burst across multiple instances.
Kill the refresh owner and verify eventual progress.
Trigger narrow and broad invalidations while measuring database connections and p99 latency.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
